title: Causal Bottleneck in the Refusal Circuit: Identifying the Token Position Where Safety Fires

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong causal chain: pinpointing the exact (layer, token) bottleneck where the refusal direction becomes load-bearing directly informs where alignment fine-tuning has maximum leverage and explains why embedding-level jailbreaks bypass prompt-level safety.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires TransformerLens, PCA/logistic probes, and causal scrubbing or activation patching. These are intermediate-level techniques with available tutorials, but combining them into a coherent causal analysis requires guided effort for beginner CS students within 30 hours.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: identify the specific (layer, token) pair whose refusal direction is necessary and sufficient, then test transfer patching. Clear success criteria and bounded experiments.

novelty.reasoning: Arditi et al. (NeurIPS 2024) demonstrated that 'Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction' across 13 open-source chat models up to 72B parameters, using contrastive pairs to identify a single difference-in-means direction. Sparse Autoencoder-based analysis of refusal features (TU Wien thesis, 2025; EMNLP 2025 Findings 'Understanding Refusal in Language Models with Sparse Autoencoders') further decomposes the refusal mechanism. The specific (layer, token) localization and causal sufficiency testing proposed by this idea overlaps heavily with these published findings, though the token-position angle adds incremental novelty beyond the layer-level and direction-level analysis.
